answer.location_description: Top-right corner of the image, roughly the top three rows and the right half of the columns. This is far from the centred nodule and lies outside the main receptive structure of the nodule detectors.
answer.shortcut_type: bright corner patch / marker-like artifact in top-right corner
answer.mechanism: Several malignancy-promoting first-layer units (10, 16, 19, and to a lesser degree 23 and 30) have a block of strongly negative weights over the top-right corner. Their weights elsewhere are a nodule-shaped center/ring pattern. Units 10, 16 and 19 feed layer-2 units with positive net effect on the logit. The main routes are via u4, u8, u13 and u15, which have positive output weights, and via negative weights onto u0, u7, u9 and u12, which have negative output weights. A bright top-right patch therefore switches these malignant units off and lowers the logit. Benign-promoting units such as 0, 8 and 25 carry mildly positive weights in the same corner. Unit 0, for example, has a strongly negative net path through u4, u8 and u15, which reinforces the push toward benign.
answer.evidence: Unit 19 rows 0-2, cols 12-23 hold weights of about -30 to -72 (for example r0: -35 -30 -49 -58 -72 -49 -69 -59 -51 -52), unlike anything else in its map. Unit 23 rows 0-2, cols 15-23 hold about -21 to -60. Unit 16 rows 0-3, cols 12-22 hold up to -56. Unit 10 rows 0-2, cols 14-21 hold up to -52. These are coherent rectangular blocks confined to one corner, not nodule-centred structure. Approximate linearised effect on the logit through layer 2: unit 10 ≈ +20k, unit 16 ≈ +31k and unit 19 ≈ +3.5k (all in integer-product units), so all three are malignancy-promoting. Unit 0, which is positive in the top-right corner (e.g., r0 cols 20-21 = 33, 43; r3 col 20 = 44), comes out at ≈ -25k, i.e. benign-promoting. A bright corner thus consistently pushes toward benign.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly uses centred centre/surround templates. Units with a compact bright core at rows 11-13, cols 10-13 surrounded by a negative ring (units 0, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 14, 15, 18, 20, 24, 25, 27, 28, 31) favour benign, i.e. small, well-circumscribed nodules. Units that respond to brightness in a wider ring around the centre (units 6, 9, 10, 12, 16, 19, 23, 30) favour malignant, i.e. larger or irregular nodules extending outward.
